verdict.headline: Iran-Hormuz ceasefire collapses as the 30-year Treasury hits a 19-year high
verdict.label: Full regime breach (3/3): Hormuz ceasefire collapsed — Iran threatens offensive posture; 30Y at 5.311% (19-yr high, 5.28% trigger breached); Brent $90.97 + WTI $85.00 (both above triggers); S&P futures -0.41%, Nasdaq futures -0.76%; FOMC Minutes tomorrow 2 PM ET; RDDT fundamental test begins at open
verdict.rationale_short: All three regime indicators are simultaneously breached for the first time this cycle. The trigger is speed, not drift: Trump's rejection of the Iran ceasefire extension on Monday sent ship traffic through Hormuz to a near-halt overnight, pushing WTI to ~$85 (+$2.68 from Monday) and Brent to ~$91 (+$2.66) — both well above their regime thresholds. Simultaneously, the 30-year Treasury crossed 5.28% to a 19-year high at 5.311%, driven by energy inflation expectations, fiscal deficit concerns, and weakening foreign Treasury demand. Consumer data entering the week was already soft: UMich sentiment fell to 51.0 (from 55.2 in July) and July retail sales came in at -0.6% MoM. Wednesday's FOMC Minutes will be parsed for stagflation acknowledgment, but they predate the ceasefire collapse — they will read as dated the moment they're released. S&P 500 futures are -0.41% premarket, Nasdaq futures -0.76%. RDDT inclusion mechanics completed at Monday's MOC auction; today's open begins the fundamental demand test.

trade_setups.thesis: 5.311% on the 30-year is a 19-year high and the first confirmed close above the 5.28% regime trigger. Three catalysts compound: (1) Hormuz oil shock passes energy inflation directly into long-run expectations; (2) Treasury auction demand weakening (recent 25-year high yield at auction); (3) Jackson Hole Aug 25 — if Warsh or Powell does not explicitly address long-end overshoot, the silence will be read as tolerance. Short TLT / long TBT on yield compression rallies is the carry-favorable position.
trade_setups.entry: Two consecutive 30Y closes above 5.28% confirms breach is structural. Any intraday compression toward 5.20% driven by dovish FOMC Minutes Wednesday 2 PM is the re-entry point for short duration.
trade_setups.invalidation: Two 30Y closes below 5.18% before Aug 25 — requires both dovish Minutes surprise and Hormuz de-escalation simultaneously.

bear_case: All three regime indicators — 30Y yield, WTI, and Brent — are simultaneously breached for the first time this cycle, and the catalyst (Hormuz ceasefire collapse) is both fast-moving and outside the Fed's toolkit. An oil shock is structurally stagflationary: it raises inflation expectations (pushing the long end higher) while simultaneously slowing consumer spending (July retail sales already -0.6% MoM, UMich sentiment at 51.0). Wednesday's FOMC Minutes predate the ceasefire collapse — they will offer no policy clarity on the week's primary risk. The fuller scenario: Hormuz disruption extends beyond four weeks, Brent reaches $95+, the 30-year rises toward 5.50% before Jackson Hole, three retail prints this week (HD Tuesday, TGT Wednesday, WMT Thursday) confirm consumer softness is a trend not a pull-forward, and NVDA's August 26 print fails to beat on both margin and guide simultaneously. In that sequence, the S&P 500's narrow leadership base provides no floor — energy adds inflation, AI/semis need multiple expansion that a 5.50% 30-year will not support. This bear case requires both Hormuz de-escalation AND two 30Y closes back below 5.18% to be invalidated.
